assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Chitin
items.clue: The substance that fungal walls are made of

items.label: Nucleolus
items.clue: Dense region that makes rRNA and assembles ribosomes

items.label: Stroma
items.clue: Fluid inside a chloroplast containing the enzymes that make sugars

items.label: Thylakoids
items.clue: Flattened membrane sacs that hold chlorophyll and are stacked into grana

questions.stem: Which statement best explains how the structure of a mitochondrion's inner membrane allows ATP to be synthesized efficiently?

options.text: Its many folds form pockets that store ATP until the rest of the cell needs it.
Its folds give a large surface area for membrane-bound steps that make ATP.
It is smooth, so ATP can pass quickly out through the folded outer membrane.
Its many folds give room to create the energy that is then stored in ATP.

questions.explanation: The inner membrane is highly convoluted. Its folds increase its surface area, so more of the membrane-bound steps of ATP synthesis can take place at once.

questions.stem: Which statement about cell walls is correct?

options.text: In bacteria, fungi and plants, the cell wall gives a structural boundary and blocks some substances.
In plants, the cell wall rather than the plasma membrane controls which solutes enter the cell.
In plants, the cell wall stops water from entering, so plant cells do not swell in pure water.
Cell walls are found around plant cells but usually not around those of fungi or bacteria.

questions.explanation: Cell walls of Bacteria, Archaea, Fungi and plants provide a structural boundary and a permeability barrier for some substances; water and many small solutes still pass through.

options.text: They are membrane-bound organelles, so they are found only in eukaryotic cells.
They copy the DNA of genes into mRNA, which then carries the copy to the cytoplasm.
They build the cell's proteins inside the nucleus, close to the genes that code for them.
They are made of rRNA and protein and are found in prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane structures made of ribosomal RNA and protein, found in the cells of all forms of life, where they synthesize proteins according to mRNA sequences.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes vacuoles in animal cells?

options.text: Animal cells have no vacuoles, as vacuoles are found only in the cells of plants.
Animal cells have many vacuoles, smaller than in plant cells, that store materials.
Animal cells have one large central vacuole that keeps them firm by turgor pressure.
Animal cells have many small vacuoles, which are sacs that hold water and nothing else.

questions.explanation: In animal cells, vacuoles are smaller and more plentiful than in plant cells, and they store cellular materials.

questions.stem: An electron micrograph of a cell shows a large amount of rough ER, a large Golgi and many small vesicles close to the cell surface. What does this cell most likely do?

options.text: It makes large amounts of lipid, using the ribosomes on its ER.
It digests engulfed bacteria, using the enzymes in its many vesicles.
It makes proteins, such as enzymes, and releases them from the cell.
It makes proteins in the Golgi, which the ER then packs into vesicles.

questions.explanation: RER makes proteins; the Golgi modifies and packages them; vesicles carry them to the surface for release.
